title: StudyStars Fact Sheet
description: A structured, age-agnostic knowledge object generated from a topic. This is the raw research output — everything we know about a topic, organized for machine consumption. It does NOT contain lesson design decisions (hooks, narrative, reflection) — those belong to the Spark. It does NOT target a specific age group — age adaptation happens at Spark generation time (Stage 2). One fact sheet per topic, three Sparks per fact sheet (one per age band).

topic.description: The topic as a noun/subject — 'Mummification', 'Photosynthesis', 'The Solar System'. NOT a question or hook — those are Spark-level decisions.

subtopic.description: Optional narrower focus within the topic. e.g. 'Organ Preservation' within 'Mummification'. Still a noun, not a question.

facts.description: The core fact set. Every activity and content slideshow draws from this pool. Each fact is tagged with what it can seed and its complexity level.

fact.description: The factual statement. Clear, concise, verifiable. Written at a neutral reading level — the Spark generator adapts vocabulary per age group.

detail.description: Expanded explanation. Used for feedback/explanations after questions, and as source material for content slideshow narration.

source.description: Where this fact comes from. For AI verification. e.g. 'Britannica', 'National Geographic'. Use 'NEEDS_VERIFICATION' if uncertain.

seedTypes.description: Which activity types this fact can seed. A fact about a date can seed sequence + quantity + fill-blank. A common misconception seeds true-false + find-the-error.

complexity.description: Complexity tier — determines which age groups can use this fact. 'core' = suitable for all ages (8-16). 'intermediate' = suitable for 11+ (skip for 8-10). 'advanced' = suitable for 14+ only. The Spark generator filters facts by complexity for its target age group.

coreFact.description: If true, this fact is essential to understanding the topic. The Spark generator MUST include it in all three age-group Sparks (adapting language, not content). Use sparingly — 3-5 facts per sheet.

facts.description: 10-25 facts provide enough material for three age-group Sparks (2-4 activities each) without repetition.

wowFacts.description: Subset of fact IDs that qualify as genuine WOW moments — jaw-dropping, counterintuitive, or emotionally resonant. WOW facts should work across all age groups (the presentation adapts, not the fact itself). The Spark generator decides WHERE to place these; the fact sheet just flags WHICH facts are wow-worthy.

misconceptions.description: Common wrong beliefs about the topic. Age-agnostic — a misconception is a misconception regardless of who believes it. These become plausible distractors for MC, and seed true-false and find-the-error activities.

claim.description: The false belief, stated as if true. e.g. 'The Great Wall of China is visible from space.'

correction.description: Why it's wrong and what's actually true.

relatedFactId.description: ID of the related correct fact.

plausibility.description: How believable the misconception is. High-plausibility misconceptions make the best distractors.

sequences.description: Ordered lists of events, steps, or stages. Seed reorder, ranking, and timeline activities.

label.description: What the sequence represents. e.g. 'The mummification process', 'Construction phases of the Great Pyramid'

sequenceType.description: What ordering principle the sequence follows.

pairs.description: Related pairs of items. Seed matching-pairs and cause-effect activities.

left.description: First item in the pair. e.g. 'Pharaoh'

relationship.description: The type of relationship between the pair.

quantities.description: Numerical facts. Seed numerical-slider and estimation activities.

question.description: The estimation question. e.g. 'How many blocks in the Great Pyramid?'

acceptableMargin.description: Percentage margin for partial credit. e.g. 0.1 = ±10%

categories.description: Groupings of items into categories. Seed categorization/sorting activities.

vocabulary.description: Key terms and definitions. Written at a neutral level — the Spark generator simplifies for younger learners. Seed flashcards, fill-in-blank, and matching pairs.

complexity.description: Mirrors the fact complexity tiers. 'natron' might be intermediate, 'desiccant' advanced.

spatialElements.description: Items that have a location on a map, diagram, or image. Seed hotspot and labeling activities.

label.description: What to identify. e.g. 'The Nile Delta'

referenceImage.description: Description of the reference image needed. e.g. 'Map of northeastern Africa'

description.description: Where/what it is on the image.

comparisons.description: Pairs or sets of things that can be compared/contrasted. Seed compare-contrast activities.

model.description: Which AI model generated this fact sheet.

qualityScore.description: AI self-assessment of fact sheet quality. 0.8+ = confident, 0.5-0.8 = some facts need checking, <0.5 = needs human review.

factCount.description: Breakdown of facts by complexity tier.
